ChronoFact: Timeline-based Temporal Fact Verification

Anab Maulana Barik, Wynne Hsu, Mong-Li Lee
School of Computing, Institute of Data Science, Centre for Trusted Internet & Community
National University of Singapore
Paper Data Poster

Abstract

Temporal claims, often riddled with inaccuracies, are a significant challenge in the digital misinformation landscape. Fact-checking systems that can accurately verify such claims are crucial for combating misinformation. Current systems struggle with the complexities of evaluating the accuracy of these claims, especially when they include multiple, overlapping, or recurring events. We introduce a novel timeline-based fact verification framework that identify events from both claim and evidence and organize them into their respective chronological timelines. The framework systematically examines the relationships between the events in both claim and evidence to predict the veracity of each claim event and their chronological accuracy. This allows us to accurately determine the overall veracity of the claim. We also introduce a new dataset of complex temporal claims involving timeline-based reasoning for the training and evaluation of our proposed framework. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in handling the intricacies of temporal claim verification.

ChronoClaims dataset

We introduce a new benchmark dataset called ChronoClaims that is designed for enhancing the accuracy and complexity of timeline-based fact verification. The dataset is originated from Wikidata. Our ChronoClaims contains 40,294 complex claims, involving up to 5 events, with both explicit and implicit temporal expressions. In addition, our dataset also contains claims with overlapping and recurring events.

ChronoFact Framework

We present ChronoFact, a novel timeline-based fact verification framework that identify events from both claim and evidence and organize them into their respective chronological timelines.

Step 1: Event Extraction and Event Encoder

  • We extract all candidate evidence sentences from relevant documents and extract events from the claim and candidate evidence sentences.
  • We employ temporal aware representation encoder model (TACV) to score and retrieve top-k evidence.
  • We utilize flan-T5 to obtain each event’s token representations. For tokens that represent date, we apply mean pooling followed by positional encoding.
  • The event’s final representation 𝐻CLS is the mean pooling over all tokens representations

Experiment

Comparative experiments on the ChronoClaims dataset. It demonstrates that ChronoFact outperforms existing state-of-the-art models by a large margin. Further analysis show that ChronoFact is better in managing complex claims with multiple events, and where the timeline of events may overlap or recur at multiple time points.

TACV remains robust on the general temporal claim verification dataset, on the realworld T-QuanTemp, despite noisy date information.
